title: Signal in the Rain
logline: During a flood-isolating storm, three community-radio operators must restore a failing broadcast network and turn their tiny station into Red Creek's lifeline.
synopsis:
As a violent storm cuts Red Creek off, June, Aria, and Noah struggle to make their aging community-radio equipment heard. The studio loses power while Aria and Noah climb the water tower with a portable antenna, and the team must choose between waiting for ideal conditions and transmitting with the one board their flooded generator can still support. Three answering chirps and a reply from the north shelter prove that the improvised network works.

Through the following day, the station grows from a fragile emergency broadcast into a community information hub. Volunteers relay road, medicine, meal, and missing-pet updates while the operators preserve room for music and humor. By the second night, nineteen reunions have been confirmed, and the steady ON AIR light embodies a town learning that attentive communication can hold it together.

act_structure.title: Signal Lost
act_structure.summary: The storm kills the studio's ON AIR light, sending Aria and Noah up the water tower to establish a fragile path back to the isolated town.
turning_points: The ON AIR light flickers once, then goes dark.
A burst of static jumps from the handheld receiver.

act_structure.title: A Community Answers
act_structure.summary: Working with flooded power and damaged equipment, the team restores one board, hears the first replies, and reframes the station as a practical relay for the whole town.
turning_points: Then three tiny chirps answer in sequence.
Red Creek station, this is north shelter. We copy your broadcast.
Announcements on the hour. Songs in between.

act_structure.title: Open Frequency
act_structure.summary: The improvised broadcast becomes a durable, two-way civic network that coordinates resources, preserves morale, and reunites nineteen people by day two.
turning_points: Community board goes out every half hour.
ARIA slides a final card onto the board: REUNIONS CONFIRMED: 19.

themes.description: The station becomes useful when its operators stop treating broadcasting as one-way performance and make room for the town to answer.
evidence: Then we stop talking and start listening.
Good evening, Red Creek. If you're out there, key once and wait.
Remember when silence meant dead air?

themes.description: Neighbors turn damaged local infrastructure into a shared network for safety, supplies, information, and reunion.
evidence: We're recording every call sign. We'll relay until sunup.
The studio wall is now covered with index cards: roads, meds, names, reunions.

themes.description: Hope is sustained through concrete, repeatable work rather than certainty, from aiming the antenna to making space for the next reunion.

narrative_arc: The story moves from communications failure and physical isolation, through the first uncertain proof of contact, to an expanding two-way network that becomes part of Red Creek's daily recovery. Repeated changes in the ON AIR light and the meaning of silence track that movement from fragility to dependable connection.
protagonist_journey: June grows from an operator testing whether a damaged station can reach anyone into the calm coordinator of a sustained community network, while Aria and Noah turn technical improvisation into shared civic purpose.
central_conflict: A storm has isolated Red Creek while flooded power and failing radio equipment threaten the team's effort to connect residents with shelters, road information, and one another.
setting_overview: Contemporary Red Creek over a storm night and the following day, moving among an aging community-radio studio, a wind-lashed water tower, the town square, and the north shelter gym.
